# Psalm 108 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)
**Translator:** SOPHIA (Council Arbiter) | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A)

---

**1** A Song. A Psalm of David. My heart is steadfast, O God! I will sing and make melody with all my being!

**2** Awake, O harp and lyre! I will awake the dawn!

**3** I will give thanks to you, O LORD, among the peoples; I will sing praises to you among the nations.

**4** For your steadfast love is great above the heavens; your faithfulness reaches to the clouds.

**5** Be exalted, O God, above the heavens! Let your glory be over all the earth!

**6** That your beloved ones may be delivered, give salvation by your right hand and answer me!

**7** God has promised in his holiness: "With exultation I will divide up Shechem and portion out the Valley of Succoth.

**8** Gilead is mine; Manasseh is mine; Ephraim is my helmet; Judah is my scepter.

**9** Moab is my washbasin; upon Edom I cast my shoe; over Philistia I shout in triumph."

**10** Who will bring me to the fortified city? Who will lead me to Edom?

**11** Have you not rejected us, O God? You do not go out, O God, with our armies.

**12** Oh grant us help against the foe, for vain is the salvation of man!

**13** With God we shall do valiantly; it is he who will tread down our foes.

---
## Council Notes

SOPHIA detected **6** significant divergence(s) in Psalm 108.

- **108:1** — EMET preserves Hebrew word-order; LOGOS restructures for English clarity; PNEUMA interprets for contemporary application.

- **108:2** — EMET preserves Hebrew word-order; LOGOS restructures for English clarity; PNEUMA interprets for contemporary application.

- **108:3** — EMET preserves Hebrew word-order; LOGOS restructures for English clarity; PNEUMA interprets for contemporary application.

- **108:4** — EMET preserves Hebrew word-order; LOGOS restructures for English clarity; PNEUMA interprets for contemporary application.

- **108:6** — EMET preserves Hebrew word-order; LOGOS restructures for English clarity; PNEUMA interprets for contemporary application.

- **108:13** — EMET preserves Hebrew word-order; LOGOS restructures for English clarity; PNEUMA interprets for contemporary application.

## Translation Notes (Select)

### EMET
- **108:1-5**: Identical to Psalm 57:7-11; vv. 6-13 identical to Psalm 60:5-12. A composite psalm joining two earlier Davidic fragments.

### LOGOS
- **108:1-13**: This psalm is a composite of Psalm 57:7-11 (praise) and Psalm 60:5-12 (petition for military victory). The combination creates a new context: praise grounds the petition.

### PNEUMA
- **108:2**: 'I'm going to wake up the dawn!' — one of the most energetic lines in the Psalms. David is so eager to praise that he'll start singing before the sun comes up.
- **108:12-13**: Human help is 'worthless' — but with God, 'we will fight and win.' The contrast is absolute. This isn't anti-human — it's recognizing where ultimate power lies.

— SOPHIA
